adminGuide.title: Site operations guide
adminGuide.intro: Common settings and workflows that guild operators often miss. Each section links directly to where you can edit it.

quickStart.title: First-time setup — 7-step checklist
quickStart.intro: Just installed the bot? Walk through these 7 steps in order before launching. Skipping any of them tends to break other features later.
quickStart.step1: Discord bot install — happens automatically when you sign up. If the bot is missing or under-permissioned, re-invite from albion-guildmanager.com/invite.
quickStart.step2: Set the Albion home guild — Settings → Events tab, search for your guild name, and link it. This anchors verification, killboard, and stats, so do this first.
quickStart.step3: Pick the operating timezone — same screen. Choose KR (KST) / EU (CET·CEST) / NA (EST·EDT) / SA (BRT) based on where most of your members live.
quickStart.step4: Configure admin roles — Settings → Permissions tab. Pick at least one Discord role that should grant admin access. Confirm one of your own roles is in the list.
quickStart.step5: Wire up the notification channel and role — Settings → Notices tab. Choose the Discord channel where events get posted and the role to mention. Without this, the channel-announce button silently fails.
quickStart.step6: Run a tiny test event — create a small dry-run event and walk through publish → notify → bulk-payout once. Future operations go smoothly after this rehearsal.
quickStart.step7: Invite your members — share the site URL (or albion-guildmanager.com/invite) and ask new members to verify their Albion nickname through the onboarding modal.

eventLifecycle.title: Event lifecycle
eventLifecycle.step1: Create event: fill in time/location/notes. Saved as draft initially.
eventLifecycle.step2: Configure parties/slots: load a template or add parties → set role, gear, and spec per slot.
eventLifecycle.step3: Publish: use the banner button to move the event to a state where members can apply.
eventLifecycle.step4: Mark battle started: press the 'Battle Started' button to lock battle_started_at. Regear window timer begins from this moment.
eventLifecycle.step5: After the event: the auto-regear job reads killboard and generates approvals. Members can submit manual regear once the window opens. Use the 'Bulk payout' button at the top of the event page to grant a fixed attendance point to every assigned member in one click.

regear.title: Regear system
regear.body: Three regear modes coexist: auto (killboard-based), event-tied manual (screenshot-based), and 'regear windows' (event-independent open intake). Setting the per-role reward cap to 0 blocks all regear claims from that role.
regear.bullet1: The auto-regear toggle is a global switch. It must be ON for killboard deaths to be converted into approvals automatically.
regear.bullet2: Slot editor has 'Exclude from auto-regear' (visible only when global ON) and 'Exclude from manual regear' (always) checkboxes for per-build opt-out.
regear.bullet3: Event-tied manual regear opens N minutes after battle start. Max screenshot 10MB, PNG/JPEG/WebP only.
regear.bullet4: Auto-generated pending rows let the claimant edit per-slot prices. Admins review at /admin/dashboard/regear.
regear.bullet5: Event-independent free regear is accepted via 'regear windows'. Open and close them at /admin/dashboard/regear-windows (or via the admin-only button on the top right of /regear) — set a title, deadline, and per-user cap. The deadline uses the same 4-part (month/day/hour/minute) input as events for mobile-friendly entry.

craftRegear.title: Crafted regear (guild boxes)
craftRegear.body: Pays out regear in crafted gear placed in numbered guild boxes instead of silver. Requesters check the 'My craft pickups' page for their box number and collect it. Multiple parts requested by the same requester are automatically funneled into the same box.
craftRegear.bullet1: In Admin → Craft regear, grant 'Crafter' permission to selected members. Only crafters can claim queued tasks.
craftRegear.bullet2: Assign each crafter a 'box range' (e.g., 1-10). The server blocks overlapping ranges between crafters automatically. Without a range, auto-assign is disabled and the crafter must enter a number manually.
craftRegear.bullet3: When a crafter opens the Deliver dialog, the system picks a box automatically: (1) reuse the same box if the requester already has one in use, otherwise (2) the smallest free number in the crafter's range. The crafter can override manually.
craftRegear.bullet4: A box only frees up once the requester collects (or it expires). Multiple parts may stack in the same box, so remind requesters to collect everything in a single trip.
craftRegear.bullet5: Per-role caps, the global box-number range (1-999), expiry days, and focus bonus all live in the 'Settings' card at the top. The 'Active tasks' panel below shows every task in flight; admins can force-cancel or convert to silver from there.

onboarding.title: Albion nickname verification
onboarding.body:
New members see an Albion server/nickname onboarding modal after login. On successful verification, both the site and Discord guild nicknames sync to the Albion name.

Verification requires an 'Albion home guild ID' set in Settings → Events tab. Without it, identities are stored but left unverified (verifiedAt=null).

A single Albion home guild can only belong to one site at a time — if another site has already claimed the same guild, that one must release it before you can verify here. During initial setup, choosing the home guild also auto-syncs the subdomain slug to the guild name. Changing the home guild later does NOT rename the subdomain.

The Stats page shows unverified/pending members. The 'Re-onboard' button clears a member's albion_* fields so the modal shows again.

timezone.title: Operating timezone
timezone.body:
The site-wide reference timezone for displaying and entering all times. During initial setup, pick KR (KST) / EU (CET·CEST) / NA (EST·EDT) / SA (BRT). All gather times, battle starts, regear deadlines, and stats follow this zone.

The same timezone drives auto-regear day boundaries, the 'today/this week' grouping in stats, and the 35-min Discord DM alert. Setting it to where the majority of your members live cuts down on "what time is that?" confusion.

You can change it any time in Settings → Events tab. Stored absolute timestamps stay the same — only how they're displayed changes.

bombSquad.title: Bomb-squad party & caller
bombSquad.body:
Bomb-squad parties use a 'members apply freely → caller approves/direct-assigns' flow. To use it:

1) Go to Settings → Permissions and configure at least one caller role.
2) Have at least one guild member with that role.
3) In the event party editor, toggle 'Bomb Squad' on and pick a caller.

Callers get a dedicated edit page at /events/{id}/party/{n} where they manage their own party's slots and members.

shop.title: Guild shop
shop.body:
Members exchange points they earned for gear. Stock syncs by copying and pasting the Albion log into the import form.

The 'discount rate' converts silver prices into point prices. 100% means silver price equals point price; 50% sells at half price.

When item prices diverge sharply from current market or look unusual, an automatic warning appears. Review and adjust those rows manually.

notifications.title: Discord notifications
notifications.body:
Notifications are delivered two ways:

- Channel announcement: posted to the event channel with a role mention. Goes out only when you press the manual button after creating or editing an event.
- Personal DM: auto-sent to assigned members before the event gather time. The lead time follows the guild default (initially 35 min, configurable in the 'Notices' tab → 'Discord notifications'); each member can override it in 'My settings', or opt out entirely.
- Approval / rejection of regear or point exchange also triggers a DM to the requester.

This requires the Discord bot to be connected first. If it isn't set up, contact the developer.

battles.title: Battle records (auto-aggregated)
battles.body: Guild-vs-guild ZvZ fights are auto-fetched from the Albion API hourly — no manual entry or screenshots required. Battles appear in the list shortly after they end. Keep these classification rules in mind so you can answer members asking why their fight isn't shown. Full ruleset lives behind the 'Show classification rules' disclosure on the /battles page.
battles.bullet1: Size buckets are based on the main opponent (single alliance or standalone guild) headcount: small 10-30, middle 31-60, large 61-100, zerg 101+.
battles.bullet2: Encounters with fewer than 10 players (ganks, straggler kills) are not ZvZ and are filtered out (10-player cutoff).
battles.bullet3: Low-engagement events (scouting, retreats, failed escapes) where K+D is far below team size are filtered too — the same Albion battle id may exist upstream but won't appear here.
battles.bullet4: A single large battle in which we fight two alliances back-to-back is split into per-opponent rows.

stats.title: Stats & monitoring
stats.body: Top/bottom point holders, event participation, shop/regear activity, and Albion verification status in one page. Use the inline 'Re-onboard' button to restart the onboarding flow for unverified members.

tips.title: Operation tips
tips.tip1: Before making big changes, run through the global toggles on the Settings page (auto-regear, auto-start, etc.) once.
tips.tip2: Save your common party layouts as templates so you can reuse them when building events. Re-saving with the same name prompts whether to overwrite the existing template.
tips.tip3: Use the party editor's 'Hide party' button to hide work-in-progress parties from members.
tips.tip4: If unexplained errors keep happening, it can be hard to fix alone — contact the developer directly.
tips.tip5: Share albion-guildmanager.com/invite as a one-click bot install link with your guild — it lands directly on the Discord bot invite page.
tips.tip6: Event gather time and regear-window deadlines now use the same 4-part (month/day/hour/minute) inputs everywhere, so mobile keypads stay consistent. Times convert to your operating timezone automatically.
tips.tip7: Reminder DMs use a guild-wide default (Settings → Notices → Discord notifications), and members can override their personal lead time anywhere from 5 to 1440 minutes in /me/settings. Useful when commute schedules differ across the roster.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.intro: Common issues and how to fix them. If you're still stuck, reach out to the developer via Telegram or Discord.
troubleshooting.p1Title: A member can't verify their Albion nickname
troubleshooting.p1Body: Make sure the 'Albion home guild' is set in Settings → Events tab — verification won't complete without it. If another site has already claimed the same Albion guild as its home, that one needs to release it first.
troubleshooting.p2Body: Confirm the home guild and the Albion server (Americas / Europe / Asia) match. The Albion API polls every 5 minutes, so kills from the last 5–10 minutes appear shortly after. Kills from unverified members may also be missing from aggregates.
troubleshooting.p3Body: Check that the global 'auto-regear' toggle is ON in Settings → Events, the per-slot 'Exclude from auto-regear' is OFF, and the per-role cap isn't 0. Auto-regear only recognizes Black Zone deaths and always creates rows in the 'pending' state — admins must approve before payout.
troubleshooting.p4Body: Channel announcements require the channel and role to be set in Settings → Notices, plus a manual 'send announcement' click after publishing. Personal DMs only arrive when the bot is in the same Discord server as the member and the member hasn't disabled notifications in /me/settings.
troubleshooting.p5Title: Battles aren't showing up in records
troubleshooting.p5Body: Encounters with fewer than 10 of our members are filtered as ganks. Low-engagement events (scouting, retreats) where K+D is far below team size are also filtered. The full ruleset is behind 'Show classification rules' on the battles page.
troubleshooting.p6Body: First confirm they're logging in with their own Discord account and are members of a Discord server the bot is in. If they aren't recognized as admin, verify the admin role configured in Settings → Permissions is actually granted to them.
troubleshooting.p7Body: 'Discount rate' converts silver to points: 100% means silver-equals-points, 50% means half-price. Large divergence from market triggers an automatic warning. Market price refresh can lag, so re-check after a few minutes.

publicFaq.q1: What Discord permissions does the bot need?
publicFaq.a1: Anyone with Manage Server permission can install. The bot uses only message-send, member-read, and role-read scopes.
publicFaq.q2: How does it pull Albion guild data?
publicFaq.a2: We pull Albion's official data every 5 minutes to refresh kill records. Loss values come from AODP (Albion Online Data Project) — a public dataset where players share market prices they collect in-game.
publicFaq.a4: In a secure cloud database. Guilds are isolated — no other guild can read your data. When a guild is deleted, the data isn't wiped immediately; it's retained for a period and then cleaned up.
publicFaq.a5: All official servers — Americas, Europe, and Asia. Pick your server during onboarding and the bot uses that server's kill records and price data.
publicFaq.q6: Can I delegate admin to other members?
publicFaq.a6: Yes. Admin is granted by Discord role: anyone with the configured admin role is automatically an admin on the site.
publicFaq.a7: One Discord server = one guild site for now. Multi-guild management is planned for a future release.
publicFaq.q8: What happens if my guild stops using it?
publicFaq.a8: Guilds with no admin login for 30+ days are flagged inactive. After further inactivity we may suspend with notice (data preserved).
publicFaq.a9: Sign-in is Discord-only — we never store passwords and never ask for Albion game credentials. All traffic is encrypted, and data is isolated per guild so other guilds can't read yours.
publicFaq.q10: How do I fully delete my guild from the site?
publicFaq.a10: Admins can request deletion from inside the site. Data is retained for 30 days, then permanently erased. You can recover during that window; after permanent deletion, member stats, event history, and kill records are gone.
publicFaq.q11: How is this different from other Albion tools (Battle Tabs, standalone Discord bots, etc.)?
publicFaq.a11: Event ops (party building, DM reminders, attendance points), reward automation (auto regear, guild shop, point exchange), and ZvZ stats are unified in one site, so you don't need spreadsheets or multiple Discord bots. We pull from Discord and the Albion kill records directly, so manual input is minimal.
publicFaq.q12: Aren't the bot's permissions too broad?
publicFaq.a12: The bot uses only message-send, member/role read, and DM-send. It doesn't read message content or touch voice channels. If permissions feel too broad, an admin can further constrain the bot role directly from Discord server settings.
publicFaq.q13: What should I do first after installing the bot?
publicFaq.a13: 1) Sign in with Discord after inviting the bot, 2) set your guild's address, 3) pick your Albion home guild, 4) assign the event-announcement channel and the active-member role, 5) review operating policies like auto-regear and the guild shop — once these five are done, members can sign in and link their Albion characters.
publicFaq.q14: What does a member do the first time they visit the site?
publicFaq.a14: Signing in with Discord starts the verification flow automatically. Enter your Albion character name to match the guild roster — once verified, your kill log, claims, and reward points start accumulating automatically. Entering a character that isn't on the guild roster leaves you in [unverified] state and some features will be limited.
publicFaq.q15: My death isn't getting picked up by auto-regear. Why?
publicFaq.a15: 1) Albion's kill records take about 30 minutes to appear in the official feed after a death — wait a moment and press 'Recheck' on the regear page. 2) Auto-regear only catches deaths in the black zone. Yellow/red-zone or non-ZvZ deaths must be submitted manually. 3) Make sure your Albion character is verified and that your guild matches the site's home guild.
publicFaq.q16: How do I customize my guild’s public page?
publicFaq.a16: Admins can edit the `/g/<slug>` page directly — banner image, banner opacity, accent color, description, recruitment status, Discord invite link, active hours, and supported languages. You can also toggle individual sections on or off (member count, battle records, weapon mix, rival guilds, admin team, and more). Use the "Edit banner" button at the top of the public page, or open the public profile settings in the admin panel.
publicFaq.q17: Which languages does the site support?
publicFaq.a17: The site UI ships in Korean, Japanese, English, and Simplified Chinese. Switch language from the top-right language menu and every page updates immediately. Note that the documentation pages (`/docs`) themselves are currently written in Korean only — additional translations are rolling out gradually.
publicFaq.q18: The public page shows the Albion English guild name. Can I show our Discord name instead?
publicFaq.a18: The public page (`/g/<slug>`) and SEO metadata always prefer your in-game Albion guild name (English) — Albion only permits English characters in guild names, and matching that name keeps the page consistent with how other players search for you or track you on the killboard. The localized Discord name is only used inside admin surfaces. To change your home guild after first setup, contact the operator (super-admin).

battleTracking.tipMatch: Battles are excluded if your home or the main opponent (largest single alliance / standalone guild) has fewer than 10 players. Size (small/medium/large/zerg) is decided by whichever side is larger.
battleTracking.tipEngagement: If your home side's (kills + deaths) is below 10% of your team size AND deaths are below 3, the battle is treated as a meaningless drive-by and hidden from display and stats.
battleTracking.tipOutcome: Win/loss is decided by total kill fame per side. More fame = win, less = loss, equal = tie.
battleTracking.tipLimitation: If you engaged both opposing alliances/guilds in the same battle, the match is split into separate rows tagged "1/2" with a shared battle marker. Newly detected battles are flagged as "Pending" until the killboard data settles, then resolved automatically.
battleTracking.rulesIntro: Battles shown here are auto-classified and filtered by the rules below. Stats, achievements, and leaderboards use the same rules.
battleTracking.rule1Body: Home = your guild (required) + every guild in the same alliance. If your guild has no alliance, only your guild is home, and everyone else is grouped as the opponent. Battles your guild did not participate in are not tracked or aggregated, even if other guilds in the same alliance fought.
battleTracking.rule2Intro: Decided by whichever is larger between home and the main opponent (the largest single alliance or standalone guild).
battleTracking.rule2CutOff: Anything under 10 is treated as ganking/stragglers and excluded entirely (the small floor = the minimum unit for proper small-scale combat).
battleTracking.rule3Body: A battle is hidden from display and stats only when BOTH conditions hold simultaneously — if only one applies, the battle is shown. Raw data is preserved, so re-classification is possible if the threshold changes. (1) Home (kills + deaths) < 10% of your team size. (2) Home deaths < 3.
battleTracking.rule3Why: Why? To prevent meaningless drive-by participation (e.g. a 70-player guild with K1/D0) from inflating win rate and stats. If deaths ≥ 3, the loss is real ("positioning failed and we wiped") so the row is kept.
battleTracking.rule4Body: Compare each side's total kill fame. More fame = win, less = loss, equal = tie. We use fame instead of raw kill count because it weights core kills against 8.3 solo trash kills correctly.
battleTracking.rule5Body: If you engaged two or more opposing alliances/standalone guilds in the same battle, the matchups are split into separate rows ("1/2" badge + same-battle marker). We do not collapse them into one row so you can see who fought whom and how.
battleTracking.rule6Body: Newly detected battles are flagged "Pending" until killboard data settles, then resolved automatically.
battleTracking.rulesLimit1: Side approximation — in a free-for-all where multiple standalone guilds (no alliance) fight individually, the opponent side may be over-aggregated (everyone outside home is treated as one side).
battleTracking.rulesLimit2: Only battles exposed via Albion's public API are tracked. Private skirmishes (small non-ZvZ ganks, etc.) are not aggregated.
battleTracking.listDescription: Public battles your guild participated in are recorded automatically. Switch sizes via tabs and filter by outcome.

shop.aodpTooltip: Market prices come from AODP (Albion Online Data Project) — a public dataset where players share market prices they capture from the game. Data density varies by server, city, and time, so when recent prices aren't available for the configured base city, the system falls back through lower quality → 14-day average → other royal cities → red-zone cities. When that fallback chain runs, the estimate may diverge from real trade value, and a "Price estimate" warning is shown.

priceWarningBuyer.quality: Price estimate: no market data for this item quality, so we substituted a lower-quality price.
priceWarningBuyer.window: Price estimate: recent market data is sparse, averaged over up to 14 days.
priceWarningBuyer.bluezone: Price estimate: no price data for the current city, so we used another Royal City's price. Actual trades may incur teleport cost and travel time.
priceWarningBuyer.redzone: Price estimate: no Royal City data at all — we used Red Zone prices (Caerleon / Brecilien). Actual value may differ significantly due to PvP risk.

priceWarningAdmin.quality: Price estimate: no data for the requested quality, so we substituted a lower-quality price.
priceWarningAdmin.window: Price estimate: recent market data is sparse, averaged over up to 14 days.
priceWarningAdmin.bluezone: Price estimate: no data for the configured city, so we used another Royal City's price.
priceWarningAdmin.redzone: Price estimate: no Royal City data at all — using Red Zone prices. Actual value may differ significantly; admin review recommended.
